w: Geelong's major regional art gallery, formerly known as Geelong Art Gallery, forms the city's Cultural Precinct together with the Geelong Library and Heritage Centre, the Geelong Arts Centre, and the Geelong Courthouse - the latter also home to Back to Back Theatre and Platform Arts.
_facts: Formerly known as Geelong Art Gallery
Forms the Cultural Precinct with the Library/Heritage Centre, Arts Centre and Courthouse
The Courthouse also houses Back to Back Theatre and Platform Arts

n: St Mary of the Angels Basilica
w: This Gothic Revival bluestone basilica on Yarra Street has carried the tallest bluestone spire in Australia since 1937 - 150 feet, the fourth-tallest non-cathedral spire in the country. Pope John Paul II made it a Minor Basilica in 2004. At 210 feet, it's the third-tallest building in Geelong.
_facts: Completed 1937; tallest bluestone spire in Australia at 150 feet
Fourth-tallest non-cathedral spire in Australia
Raised to Minor Basilica status by Pope John Paul II in 2004
Third-tallest building in Geelong at 210 feet

n: St. John the Baptist Macedonian Orthodox Church, Geelong
w: A Macedonian Orthodox church on the outskirts of Batesford, near Geelong, with construction begun in 1971 and the building consecrated in 1978 - a marker of the Macedonian community that settled in the area and still worships here.
_facts: Construction began 1971, consecrated 1978
Located at Batesford on Geelong's outskirts
Serves the local Macedonian community

w: An 8-hectare public park on the banks of the Barwon River in the suburb of Newtown, opened in 1973, mixing open parkland with lakes and wetlands - a quiet green pocket a short walk from central Geelong's cafes and streets.
s: Wetland park on the Barwon River, Newtown
_facts: 8 hectares (20 acres) on the Barwon River in Newtown
Opened in 1973
Mix of parkland, lakes and wetlands

w: A 250-hectare wildlife reserve near Lara, bought by the Victorian government in 1959 for research and captive breeding of species threatened in the state, including the brolga and bush stone-curlew. Opened to the public in 1991, it's now a wetland refuge managed by Parks Victoria, focused on environmental education.
s: Wildlife breeding sanctuary north of Geelong
_facts: 250ha reserve near Lara, purchased 1959 for wildlife research
Bred threatened species: brolga, magpie goose, Australian bustard, bush stone-curlew
Opened to the public in 1991; managed by Parks Victoria

w: An upland ridge on Geelong's western outskirts, sloping steeply down to the Barwon River on its northern side and more gently to the coastal lowland in the south. The area covers the localities of Gnarwarre, Barrabool and Ceres, straddling three local government areas.
s: Ridge west of Geelong straddling three council areas
_facts: Upland ridge on the south side of the Barwon River
Covers Gnarwarre, Barrabool and Ceres
Straddles the City of Greater Geelong, Surf Coast Shire and Golden Plains Shire

w: A road bridge and a separate footbridge across the Barwon River, linking Barwon Heads to Ocean Grove - the only crossing of the river between Geelong itself and the river mouth at Barwon Heads.
s: The only river crossing near Barwon Heads
_facts: Road bridge plus a separate pedestrian bridge over the Barwon River
Links Barwon Heads and Ocean Grove
Only crossing of the Barwon River between Geelong and the river mouth
